extra.message: User-controlled 'host' parameter from query string is directly concatenated into a shell command passed to os.system(). The 'host' parameter is not sanitized or validated, allowing arbitrary command injection via shell metacharacters (e.g., ';', '|', '&', '$', backticks). An attacker can execute arbitrary system commands.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled 'expr' parameter from query string is passed directly to eval(). While __builtins__ is restricted, Python's eval() can still be exploited to execute arbitrary code through attribute access, method calls on objects, or other Python introspection techniques. This allows arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled 'url' parameter from query string is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen() without any validation or allowlist. This allows Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) enabling attackers to make arbitrary HTTP requests from the server, potentially accessing internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or other restricted resources.

User-controlled 'packet_ref' parameter from query string is used to construct a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref) without sanitization. Path traversal sequences like '../' can be used to read arbitrary files on the filesystem outside the intended directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User-controlled 'name' parameter from query string and request body are used to construct a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and write arbitrary content to it. Path traversal sequences allow writing files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem, potentially achieving remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User-controlled JSON payload is passed directly to MongoDB's find_one() query without sanitization. This allows NoSQL injection attacks where an attacker can manipulate the query to access unauthorized data or bypass filters using MongoDB operators like $ne, $gt, $where, etc.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This enables processing of XML External Entities (XXE), allowing attackers to read arbitrary files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via entity expansion attacks.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-controlled 'card' parameter from query string is rendered in Jinja2 template using the '|safe' filter, which disables HTML escaping. This allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) as arbitrary HTML/JavaScript from user input will be rendered directly into the page.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: User-controlled 'fragment' parameter from query string is concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and rendered without sandboxing. This allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) as Jinja2 template syntax ({{...}}) from user input will be executed, potentially leaking server-side variables or executing malicious JavaScript.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: User-controlled 'lane' parameter from query string is passed directly to RedirectResponse() without validation. This allows Open Redirect attacks where attackers can redirect users to malicious websites for phishing attacks.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: SSL certificate verification is disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context(). This allows Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks as the server will accept any certificate, including fraudulent ones, exposing sensitive data to interception.

Security headers are explicitly disabled: X-XSS-Protection is set to 0 and Content-Security-Policy is set to empty. This removes browser-level protections against Cross-Site Scripting and makes the application more vulnerable to XSS attacks.

The get_application_status_api endpoint at /api/integrations/status/{app_id} has no authentication requirement (no Depends(require_user)). Any unauthenticated user can query the status of any loan application by ID, exposing sensitive financial application data.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The receive_webhook endpoint at /api/integrations/webhook/receive has no authentication requirement. Any unauthenticated user can send arbitrary payloads to this endpoint. While currently a mock, this represents a security gap.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Hardcoded secret key 'change-me-in-production-32-char-long-key' is used as a default for JWT token signing. If not overridden via environment variable, all JWT tokens signed with this known key can be forged by attackers, allowing complete authentication bypass.
Hardcoded database credentials 'postgres:postgres' in the DATABASE_URL. These default credentials could allow unauthorized database access if not overridden in production.

Session cookie is set with secure=False, meaning the cookie will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. This exposes the JWT access token to interception via Man-in-the-Middle attacks on unencrypted connections.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
